---
title: "Measurement-Error Models and REPAIR"
subtitle: "Source resolution, cross-trial shared-error moments, and participant-cluster inference beyond diagonal M-MOMS"
---

::: {.callout-note title="How this chapter relates to Step 6 in `medusa`"}
In `medusa`, `decon_connectivity_repair(..., shared_error = "auto")` implements per-trial M-MOMS predictor disattenuation, task-free cross-parcel `shared_noise_loading` / `unit_error_cor` error-moment subtraction (`err_xy`), and HKSJ participant-level random-effects pooling ([Step 6](../medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd)). This chapter investigates what lies **beyond** diagonal per-trial M-MOMS: unequal regional trial resolution ($K_S \neq K_T$), full cross-trial error covariance blocks ($\Omega_{SS}, \Omega_{ST}$), likelihood-only finite-basis trial reconstruction, and participant-cluster estimating equations.
:::

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
s <- read.csv("simulation_summary.csv", check.names = FALSE)
get_result <- function(scenario, method, term = "Connectivity", column = "mean") {
  x <- s[s$scenario == scenario & s$method == method & s$term == term, column]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1)
  x
}
f <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
pct <- function(x) paste0(f(100 * x, 1), "%")
bridge <- read.csv("likelihood_bridge_checks.csv")
joint <- read.csv("joint_gaussian_example.csv")
stopifnot(all(s$attempts == 400), all(s$failures == 0))
```

## Summary of Findings

**Attaching diagonal trial SEs to ordinary M-MOMS disattenuates independent white measurement noise, but full latent connectivity inference faces three deeper structural requirements:** unbiased source resolution, cross-parcel/cross-trial shared-error moments, and participant-cluster uncertainty calibration.

- **Recover an unbiased source mean (or model resolution explicitly):** Regularized continuous deconvolution yields $\mathbb{E}[\widehat{z}_{g} \mid \theta_g] = K_g \theta_g$ with $K_g \neq I$. In our controlled unequal-resolution experiment ($K_S \neq K_T$), full noise-moment subtraction alone estimated connectivity as **`r f(get_result("Different resolution","Full moments, cluster SE"))`** when truth was `0.550`. Inverting known, well-conditioned resolution operators restored recovery to **`r f(get_result("Different resolution","Resolution inverse + full moments"))`**.
- **Propagate shared errors and cluster at the participant level:** Under unbiased source measurements with strong serial ($0.55$) and shared cross-parcel ($0.45$) Gaussian noise, the full cross-trial corrected-score estimator recovered **`r f(get_result("Serial + shared Gaussian","Full moments, cluster SE"))`**. Participant-cluster intervals covered truth in **`r pct(get_result("Serial + shared Gaussian","Full moments, cluster SE",column="coverage"))`** of repetitions, whereas row-based intervals covered only **`r pct(get_result("Serial + shared Gaussian","Full moments, row SE",column="coverage"))`**.
- **Respect finite-participant limits:** With only 12 participants, asymptotic cluster sandwich intervals undercovered (`r pct(get_result("Few participants","Full moments, cluster SE",column="coverage"))` connectivity coverage)—motivating the dispersion-scaled finite-sample $t$-interval (HKSJ) pooling used in `medusa::decon_connectivity_repair()`.

## 1. Define the neural relationship and the measurement relationship

For participant $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$ and trial $i$, define a centered task modulator $x_{si}$ and latent seed/target trial amplitudes $(\theta_{S,si}, \theta_{T,si})$ matching Step 6:

$$
\theta_{T,si}=\alpha_s+\beta_S \theta_{S,si}+\beta_x x_{si}
               +\beta_P (x_{si}\theta_{S,si})+\eta_{si}.
$$

$\beta_S$ is the seed–target association at $x=0$; $\beta_P$ is its task modulation (PPI). Across all trials of participant $s$, the linear trial-readout measurement interface is:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}\widehat{z}_{S,s}\\\widehat{z}_{T,s}\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}K_{S,s}&0\\0&K_{T,s}\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\theta_{S,s}\\\theta_{T,s}\end{bmatrix}
+\begin{bmatrix}u_s\\v_s\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\!\begin{pmatrix}u_s\\v_s\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}\Omega_{SS,s}&\Omega_{ST,s}\\
\Omega_{ST,s}^{\top}&\Omega_{TT,s}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Classical additive measurement-error correction assumes $K_S = K_T = I$. In addition, **PPI products and trial smoothing do not commute**:

$$
K\,\operatorname{diag}(x)\theta_S \ne \operatorname{diag}(x)K \theta_S.
$$

Multiplying a smoothed or within-run decorrelated (ZCA-whitened) seed by the task modulator $x$ afterward does not match smoothing the latent interaction—which is why `decon_connectivity_repair()` defaults to `use_whitened = FALSE`.

## 2. Three workable measurement models

### A. Likelihood-only coefficients in a modest source basis

Represent each parcel $g$'s BOLD run series using a prespecified, low-dimensional neural event basis passed through its learned HRF:

$$
y_g=G_g \theta_g+Z_g\gamma_g+\varepsilon_g,
\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_g)=\Sigma_g.
$$

When $G_g$ has full column rank (e.g., well-spaced trial impulses or low-dimensional epoch bases) and is fit via unpenalized GLS in whitened coordinates,

$$
\widehat{z}_g=B_g y_g,\qquad B_g G_g=I,
\qquad \mathbb{E}(\widehat{z}_g\mid \theta_g)=\theta_g,
\qquad \Omega_{gg}=B_g\Sigma_g B_g^{\top},
\qquad \Omega_{ST}=B_S\Sigma_{\varepsilon_S,\varepsilon_T}B_T^{\top}.
$$

This provides an exact unbiased additive measurement-error model ($K_g = I$), closely paralleling likelihood-only coefficient reconstruction in REPAIR ([Abdulrahman & Henson, 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4692520/)). In `likelihood_only_bridge.R` (16 source amplitudes, 180 BOLD volumes, distinct regional HRFs, shared/serial AR noise), trial operators satisfy $BG = I$ to **`r format(max(bridge$value[1:2]),scientific=TRUE,digits=3)`**, and a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo check matches analytical source SDs within **`r pct(bridge$value[7])`**. Its trade-off is design conditioning: rapid jittered event schedules or omitted sustained activity can make unpenalized $G_g$ collinear or misspecified.

### B. De-penalize only identifiable contrasts

For a linear Gaussian posterior with precision $C_{\rm post}^{-1} = J + P_{\rm prior}$, likelihood information $J$ is recoverable only on subspaces where $J$ is well-conditioned. In `likelihood_only_bridge.R`, the full 180-column continuous convolution matrix has numerical rank **`r f(bridge$value[5],0)`**, confirming why continuous TR-grid deconvolution cannot simply drop its penalty globally without projecting onto identifiable trial/window contrasts first.

### C. Retain resolution $K_S, K_T$ inside a joint latent Gaussian model

When unshrinking is ill-conditioned, $K_S$ and $K_T$ can be retained explicitly inside a joint Gaussian marginal likelihood over $(\widehat{z}_{S,s}, \widehat{z}_{T,s}) \mid x_s$. In `joint_gaussian_demo.R` (known unequal $K_S \neq K_T$ and known $\Omega$), maximum likelihood recovered connectivity **`r f(joint$estimate[1])`** (truth `0.550`) and PPI **`r f(joint$estimate[3])`** (truth `0.350`) with a positive-definite Hessian, trading stronger distributional assumptions and computation for exact handling of non-identity resolution.

<details>
<summary>Gaussian conditional-mean calibration variant</summary>

Let $m_S = \mathbb{E}(\theta_S \mid \widehat{z}_S, x)$ under a Gaussian seed prior. With independent regional errors,
$$
\mathbb{E}(\widehat{z}_T \mid \widehat{z}_S, x) = K_T\{Z\gamma + \beta_S m_S + \beta_P\operatorname{diag}(x)m_S\},
$$
requiring design columns $K_T m_S$ and $K_T \operatorname{diag}(x) m_S$ rather than multiplying $m_S$ by $x$ after applying $K_T$, plus an explicit shared-noise regression term $\Omega_{TS}(K_S V_S K_S^\top + \Omega_{SS})^{-1}(\widehat{z}_S - K_S \mu_S)$ whenever $\Omega_{TS} \neq 0$.

</details>

## 3. Full cross-trial corrected-score estimating equations

For unbiased trial readouts ($K_S = K_T = I$), form participant $s$'s centered trial design $\widehat{X}_s = X_s + U_s$ for columns $[\theta_S,\, x,\, \theta_S x]$ and define full cross-trial error moments $\Psi_s = \mathbb{E}(U_s^\top U_s)$ and $c_s = \mathbb{E}(U_s^\top v_s)$ (including run-centering projections applied consistently to both data and $\Omega_{SS}, \Omega_{ST}$). Solving the summed participant corrected score ([Nakamura, 1990](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/77/1/127/271070); [Buonaccorsi, 1996](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/83/2/433/289324)):

$$
q_s(\beta)=\widehat{X}_s^{\top}\widehat{z}_{T,s}-c_s
       -(\widehat{X}_s^{\top}\widehat{X}_s-\Psi_s)\beta,
\qquad \sum_{s=1}^S q_s(\widehat\beta)=0,
$$

yields an unbiased estimating equation $\mathbb{E}[q_s(\beta_0)] = 0$ with participant-cluster sandwich variance:

$$
\widehat V=H^{-1}\left[\frac{S}{S-1}\sum_{s=1}^S
q_s(\widehat\beta)q_s(\widehat\beta)^{\top}\right]H^{-\top},
\quad
H=\sum_{s=1}^S(\widehat{X}_s^{\top}\widehat{X}_s-\Psi_s).
$$

<details>
<summary>Prototype interface (`measurement_error_models.R`)</summary>

```r
source("measurement_error_models.R")
fit <- fit_corrected(blocks, mode = "full")
stopifnot(fit$ok)
fit$estimate  # neural association, task main effect, PPI
fit$se        # participant-cluster score SEs
```

The prototype refuses indefinite corrected information matrices rather than silently regularizing unidentified designs.

</details>

## 4. Conditional simulation benchmarks (400 repetitions per scenario)

Each scenario simulates 400 repetitions of $S = 60$ participants (`Few participants` uses $S = 12$) with 24 trials per participant, true connectivity $\beta_S = 0.55$, task main effect $\beta_x = 0.25$, and PPI $\beta_P = 0.35$ (`Null` sets $\beta_S = \beta_P = 0$), under serial trial error correlation $0.55$ and shared cross-region error correlation $0.45$.

![Mean coefficient bias across three stress scenarios. Bars show plus/minus 1.96 Monte Carlo SE; horizontal scales differ across columns. The oracle uses true neural amplitudes. Empty Undo K rows mean that method was only evaluated in the unequal-resolution scenario.](bias.png){#fig-bias fig-alt="Noise correction recovers slopes under unbiased measurements, but remains biased with unequal resolution; the stable resolution inverse restores recovery in the controlled example."}

![Coverage of nominal 95% normal intervals. Bars are exact binomial 95% intervals for the Monte Carlo coverage probability, not individual-model confidence intervals. The dashed reference is 95%; all horizontal axes span 0–100%. Full + row SE and Full + cluster SE have the same point estimate.](coverage.png){#fig-coverage fig-alt="Participant-cluster inference improves connectivity coverage with serial errors; neither interval method fixes unequal-resolution bias. Undoing known stable resolution restores coverage in this controlled case."}

```{r key-results}
show <- s[s$method %in% c("Full moments, cluster SE", "Resolution inverse + full moments") &
  s$scenario %in% c("Serial + shared Gaussian", "Serial + shared t5", "Different resolution", "Few participants"), ]
show <- show[order(show$scenario, show$method, show$term), ]
kable(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = show$scenario,
    Method = show$method,
    Effect = show$term,
    Mean = round(show$mean, 3),
    Bias = round(show$bias, 3),
    Coverage = pct(show$coverage),
    `Coverage MCSE` = pct(show$coverage_mcse),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  caption = "Selected conditional simulation benchmarks (400 repetitions per row)."
)
```

Three practical lessons bridge these benchmarks back to empirical `medusa` analyses:

1. **Omitting shared cross-parcel error creates severe false connectivity:** Under `Null serial + shared`, ignoring $\Omega_{ST}$ (`Zero shared covariance`) falsely rejects in **`r pct(get_result("Null serial + shared","Zero shared covariance",column="rejection"))`** of repetitions, whereas subtracting $\Omega_{ST}$ drops connectivity false positives to **`r pct(get_result("Null serial + shared","Full moments, cluster SE",column="rejection"))`**—directly motivating `shared_error = "auto"` in Step 6.
2. **Unequal source resolution requires matched HRF/inverse scales:** When two parcels have markedly different effective smoothing ($K_S \neq K_T$), naive attenuation and resolution distortion can partially cancel (`r f(get_result("Different resolution","Naive"))`) while variance-only disattenuation overshoots (`r f(get_result("Different resolution","Full moments, cluster SE"))`). Keep regularization policies matched across seed and target parcels and control shared task main effects carefully ([Cole et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6422749/)).
3. **Small-$S$ cohorts require finite-sample $t$/HKSJ adjustments:** Normal asymptotic cluster SEs undercover at $S = 12$ ([MacKinnon, Nielsen & Webb, 2022](https://arxiv.org/html/2205.03285v1)), which is why `decon_connectivity_repair()` uses HKSJ $t$-intervals over participant slopes rather than normal row or unadjusted cluster $z$-intervals.
